RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for  ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the April 29, 2008/Vaisakha 9, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance;
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
159
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Losses incurred by PSU, oil
companies and refineries
*501. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) what is the value of losses incurred
by PSU, oil producing companies and oil
refining companies during 2006-07 and
2007-08, due to Government control on
petroleum prices, and
(b) in what ratio have these losses been
absorbed by oil producing companies, oil
refining companies and Government
respectively?
Capital investment by oil companies
in foreign countries
†*502. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
oil companies are making capital investment
in construction of basic facilities in other
countries;
(b) if so, the names of such companies
whose proposals to make capital
investment in different countries are under
consideration till now, the details of amount
involved and the names of such countries;
and
(c) the estimated percentage of profit
from this capital investment?
Buddhist heritage centre in Orissa
*503. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Sri Lanka
has asked its Indian counterpart to develop
Buddhist sites in the Southern sector,

160
i.e. Andhra Pradesh and Orissa, to facilitate
Buddhist tourists to visit such heritage
centres;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the action plan of
Government to develop such Buddhist
heritage centres in Orissa to promote
Buddhist tourism in that State?
Role of private companies in Civil
Aviation
*504. PROF. P. J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the expansion of Metro
Airports has been entrusted to private
companies;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether ground handling and
ensuring security at these airports have also
been entrusted to them; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Multiple airports in big cities
*505. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to build more
than one airport in big cities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any such policy has been
framed;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Interlinking of rivers as National
Project
*506. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) what is preventing Government to
declare inter-linking of rivers in the country
as a National Project;
(b) whether Government would declare
any time bound action plan in order to
implement the National Project; and
(c) if so, whether Government is
considering to make a provision in the
Eleventh Five Year Plan for the funds
required for the project?
Permission to NetJet for operating in
India
*507. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARW AL: Will the Minister of  CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has given
permission to NetJet to operate in India
with an Indian strategic partner;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the terms
and conditions of the permission granted;
(c) whether security clearance from
Government has been obtained by NetJet
for foray into Indian market; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Construction of Pulichintala Project
in Andhra Pradesh
*508. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of
W ATER RESOURCES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that to provide
irrigation facilities to some of the districts

161
of Andhra Pradesh, the State Government
is constructing the Pulichintala Project
across Krishna river;
(b) if so, whether any slippages have
been noticed while constructing the project;
(c) if so, the details of cost and time
overruns, the reasons for slippages and the
measures taken to arrest them along with
their impact;
(d) the districts of Andhra Pradesh
which would be covered by the project;
and
(e) by when the project would be
completed and total area of land that would
be irrigated?
Revision of pay in Public Sector
Banks/Insurance Companies
*509. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the pay revision of Public
Sector Banks and Insurance Companies is
due and the employees and workers'
organisations have already given their
demand;
(b) if so, by when Government is going
to start the negotiation with these
organisations; and
(c) whether these organisations of
employees and officers are demanding long
term settlement for five years?
Approval of CCEA for investment by
foreign companies
*510. SHRI SYED AZEEZ
PASHA:
SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARW AL:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether foreign companies whose
original investment exceeded Rs. 600 crores
in the mid 90s were referred to the Cabinet
Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)
for final approval;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether even a small increase in
investment or even minor amendment in
the letter of approval requires applications
by such companies to be referred to CCEA;
(d) whether if these early entrants had
instead entered India today in sectors where
100 per cent foreign equity is permitted
they would have been  entitled to automatic
approval; and
(e) whether his Ministry will
recommend liberalization of rules on this
count to foreign investors who entered India
in the early 1990s?
Employment of foreign pilots
*511. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a shortage of pilots
in the Indian Civil Aviation sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total requirement of pilots by
Civil Aviation sector and how Government
proposes to meet the requirements;
(d) whether the Director General of Civil
Aviation (DGCA) has invited foreign pilots
to work for Indian Civil Aviation sector;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Facilities for physically challenged
air-passengers
*512. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian carriers are opposing

162
the decision to provide mandatory free
facilities to physically challenged
passengers;
(b) if so, whether the Director General
of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which had earlier
proposed this in a draft civil aviation
requirement, has re-sent its proposal to the
Ministry with the views of Airlines;
(c) if so, whether Government has taken
any final decision in this regard; and
(d) if so, whether any directions have
been issued to all the Indian Carriers to
continue the free facilities to the physically
challenged passengers?
Demand for LPG cylinders
*513. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of total demands received
from each State during the current year till
now for the supply of LPG cylinders under
the Public Distribution System alongwith
the quantum of allotment made to each State
every month;
(b)  the demand received from Gujarat
and allotment made to it;
(c) whether the said demands have been
totally fulfilled; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Protection of historical monuments in
Maharashtra
*514. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received
any proposals from the State Government
of Maharashtra for financial assistance for
the protection of historical monuments
there;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
the location-wise details of each project;
and
(c) what is the status of these proposals
and the funds allocated for these
monuments during last two years?
Central control over rivers and
ground water
*515. SHRI MAHENDRA
MOHAN:
DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA
A. HEPTULLA:
Will the Minister of W ATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
Second Administrative Reforms
Commission has suggested framing of
radical national law to centralize control
over rivers and ground water in order to
address emerging conflicts;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal and
Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether any serious efforts have
been made by Government to find out
solution of Cauvery water dispute so that
conflicts between the people of States could
be avoided and matter does not become
political; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and position
taken by both the States in this regard?
Roadmap on Broad Framework of
GST
*516. SHRI DARA SINGH:
SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Empowered Committee
of State Finance Ministers for setting up

163
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
of a model and roadmap on Board
Framework of Goods and Services Tax
(GST) has finalized its report, till date;
(b) if so, by when the Committee's Final
Report on Value Added Tax (V AT) is likely
to be submitted to Government; and
(c) how much time Government is likely
to take to examine/implement the
recommendations made by the Committee,
throughout the country?
Reduction of Government stake in
banks
†*517. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Committee
constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri
Anwarul Hoda, Member, Planning
Commission, has advised Government to
reduce its present stake in the banks;
(b) if so, the details thereof, the average
stake of Government in banks at present
and the percentage stake recommended by
the abovesaid Committee; and
(c) the benefits expected as a result of
reduction of Government stake?
Tourism project in Gujarat
*518. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will
the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Gujarat has sent some proposals for certain
tourism projects to the Central
Government for approval/sanction; and
(b) if so, the number of projects which
have been cleared and the number of projects
which have not been cleared so far?
Resentment against Sixth Pay
Commission Report
*519. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central
Government Employees Unions have
announced that the Sixth Pay Panel Report
is unacceptable to them;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the Sixth Pay Commission
has made some amendments in its report;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
New Exploration Licensing Policy
*520. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUAR: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) what are the details of the New
Exploration Licensing Policy;
(b) what are the details of the projects
under which exploration of oil and gas is
being carried out under the new Policy,
State-wise;
(c) what are the details of the agencies
involved; and
(d) what are the details of the success
that has been achieved so far?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 23rd April, 2008 Secretary-General.
Vaisakha 3, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 504, 505, 507, 511, 512,
Corporate Affairs :—
Culture : 514,
Finance : 509, 510, 516, 517, 519,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises :—
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 501, 502, 513, 520,
Tourism : 503, 518,
Water Resources : 506, 508, 515.
164
MGIPMRND—1650RS—23.04.2008.
